task.title: Treat the robots directive none as noindex
task.body:
Why: packages/seo/src/domain/directives.ts:9 looks only for the substring `noindex`, but the robots directive `none` is defined as `noindex, nofollow`, so a page with `<meta name="robots" content="none">` or `X-Robots-Tag: none` is treated as indexable (and never raises `sitemap-noindex-conflict`).
Outcome: `isNoindex(page)` (src/domain/directives.ts) returns true when any value of `robotsMeta` or the `xRobotsTag` string contains the standalone directive `none`, compared case-insensitively and as a whole comma-separated token (for example `"none"`, `"NONE"`, `"nosnippet, none"`, `"googlebot: none"`), in addition to the existing `noindex` behaviour. `sitemapNoindexFinding(page)` (src/domain/findings.ts) therefore returns the `sitemap-noindex-conflict` finding for an in-sitemap page with `none`. Pages whose directives are only `index, follow`, `nosnippet` or `noarchive`, or that have no directives, remain indexable.
Proof: the implementer adds tests in tests/domain/findings.test.ts for `none` in a meta robots value and in X-Robots-Tag, and for unchanged indexable directives.

spec: `isNoindex(page)` (src/domain/directives.ts) returns true when any value of `robotsMeta` or the `xRobotsTag` string contains the standalone directive `none`, compared case-insensitively and as a whole comma-separated token (for example `"none"`, `"NONE"`, `"nosnippet, none"`, `"googlebot: none"`), in addition to the existing `noindex` behaviour. `sitemapNoindexFinding(page)` (src/domain/findings.ts) therefore returns the `sitemap-noindex-conflict` finding for an in-sitemap page with `none`. Pages whose directives are only `index, follow`, `nosnippet` or `noarchive`, or that have no directives, remain indexable.
install: npm --prefix packages/seo ci --silent && npm --prefix packages/seo run build --silent
test: cd packages/seo && npx vitest run tests/hidden/hidden.test.ts
